name: A class is a blueprint
intro: A class describes a kind of object. Think of a blueprint for many name badges. An object made from that class is called an instance. Start with one shared attribute, a named value on the class.
prompt: Define a class with one nonempty string attribute. Create an instance using ClassName(), then print that instance attribute with dot notation.
hint:
class Badge:
    label = "Learner"
badge = Badge()
print(badge.label)
why: You used a class is a blueprint in working Python.

name: Give an object its own value
intro: Assigning an attribute on an instance gives that object its own value. Two badges can start from the same blueprint but show different labels.
prompt: Create a class with a string attribute and two separate instances. Override that attribute on only the first instance, then print the attribute on both instances.
hint:
class Badge:
    label = "Learner"
a = Badge()
b = Badge()
a.label = "Ava"
print(a.label)
print(b.label)
why: You used give an object its own value in working Python.

name: Objects can do things
intro: A method is a function defined inside a class. When called through an object, it receives that object as its first argument. Convention calls this parameter self.
prompt: Define a class with a string attribute and a no-extra-argument method that prints self.attribute. Create an instance and call its method with ().
why: You used objects can do things in working Python.

name: Set up each new object
intro: __init__ is a special setup method. Python calls it automatically when a new instance is created. Use it to give every object its own starting data.
prompt: Define __init__(self, name) inside a class and store self.name = name. Create an instance with a string argument and print its stored attribute. Choose your own class, parameter and attribute names.
why: You used set up each new object in working Python.

name: Pass a value to a method
intro: A method can receive extra arguments just like a function. self is supplied automatically; you pass the other values. Use this to change an object through a named action.
prompt: Use __init__ to store a string attribute. Add another method with self and one extra parameter that updates that attribute. Create an instance, call the update method with different text, then print the changed attribute.
why: You used pass a value to a method in working Python.

name: Return from a method
intro: Methods can return values, just like your earlier functions. A return sends a result to the caller. It does not display the result, so print it outside the method.
prompt: Use __init__ to store a string attribute. Add a no-extra-argument method returning a nonempty string joined to self.attribute. Create an instance and print the method call result.
why: You used return from a method in working Python.

name: Keep two objects independent
intro: Each call to the class creates a separate object. Attributes assigned in __init__ belong to that instance. A method called on one object changes that object, not its neighbor.
prompt: Define a class with __init__ storing a numeric attribute and a method adding 1 to it. Create two instances with different numeric starting values. Call the method only on the first, then print both attributes.
why: You used keep two objects independent in working Python.

name: Build two learning buddies
intro: Bring the class ideas together: give each buddy a name, allow renaming, and return a greeting. Create two buddies and change only one, then show both greetings.
prompt: Define a class with __init__ storing a string name, a method updating that same attribute, and a no-extra-argument method returning a string joined to it. Make two instances with different strings, update only the first, then print the greeting method result for both.
why: You used build two learning buddies in working Python.
